b2e: Dibii mbili haskali karka moro mooyi.
Komelopó chiwapa khabari kuwa dughaaghi fiile.
Duniyaani kilaa iintu uwone ana s o uwone ana ni uso wa mojiitu.
Hamadi walishize shteko dhakh dhakh dhakh.
Omari dukaye huza zoombo ghaali kana dahabu.
Omari upen a udulis a waantu.
e2b: His complaints have no end.’ (A proverbial saying.)
He goes away leaving this  fox to watch the child.
The boil, infected wound is  stinging like a needle [i.e. like being pricked by a needle].
Can you stay awake the whole  night through?

The one who cannot take of a wife is one who could be her father (lit. who gives birth to her).’ (A proverb that conveys the idea that poor provider for his wife is someone much older than her, old enough to be her father.)
They do whatever the government wants, if these things that they do will harm them or harm their relatives or others.
So, pray for me that God send me in peace and bring me back in peace.
[st.] ‘I implore God to obliterate my sins/ may God pardon my sins
And it became clear to you that there is no God.
He exposed the government’s lies, deceptions, etc.
